runs.text: Choose u to differentiate and dv to integrate; then compute du and one antiderivative v.
Repeated use is effective when differentiation simplifies a polynomial or eventually cycles. A tabular layout is bookkeeping for repeated applications, not a separate theorem.

items.text: For the definite formula, u and v should satisfy the standard differentiability and integrability conditions on [a,b].
Choose dv only when it has a usable antiderivative.
LIATE is a heuristic for choosing u, not a validity condition.

examples.title: Integrate a polynomial times an exponential

items.text: Keep the minus sign before the remaining integral.
For definite integrals, evaluate the boundary product as well as the remaining integral.
